_: Reference file. Not read by anything — it exists to show every field, since JSON has no comments. Copy the shape you need into validation.json.

commands.run: npm run gen:api && git diff --exit-code src/api/generated
commands._why: freshness check: regenerate from the contract and fail if what is committed differs — this is what catches generated types that went stale

boundaries._why: commands: [] means there is no executable validation here. The runner reports that and never substitutes another boundary's suite.

_duplication._why: jscpd is the one tool the harness asks you to install. It is a self-contained Rust binary with no runtime, covers 224 formats, and tokenizes rather than executes — so it needs none of the project's toolchain and runs on a freshly cloned repo before anything is installed. Add this command to any boundary that holds source code.
_duplication._install: irm https://jscpd.dev/install.ps1 | iex   (or: npm install -g jscpd — npm only delivers the binary, Node is not used at runtime)
_duplication._tuning: --threshold 0 fails on any duplication and is too strict for real code. Raise it against the actual project until it reports what you would want to know and stays quiet otherwise. A detector that fires constantly gets ignored, which is worse than not having one.
_duplication._limits: Catches type 1-3 clones: copied, renamed, lightly edited. Does NOT catch type 4 — the same idea implemented differently. That case has no reliable tool and only a fresh-eyes review of the diff finds it.
_duplication._not_adopted: The jscpd MCP server and its dry-refactoring skill are deliberately left out. The MCP server would add tool definitions to every request for an occasional lookup. The skill guides toward eliminating duplication, which contradicts this harness's rule to prefer duplication over the wrong abstraction.

_fields.paths: globs that map a changed file to this boundary
_fields.consumedBy: other boundaries that depend on this one. Editing this boundary also runs their validation — this is what stops a backend change from silently breaking the frontend.
_fields.commands[].run: the literal command, exactly as declared. Never substituted, never guessed.
_fields.commands[].prerequisites: what must exist for the command to be meaningful. Missing prerequisite yields BLOCKED, never FAIL — so a broken environment is not mistaken for broken code.
_fields.unmappedPathPolicy: report | ignore. A changed file matching no boundary is reported, so gaps in the manifest surface instead of passing silently.

_outcomes: UNMAPPED  - the path matches no boundary. Reported; no command guessed.
NO CHECKS - the boundary exists but declares no commands. Reported.
BLOCKED   - a prerequisite is missing. Never PASS, never FAIL.
FAIL      - a command exited non-zero. Output truncated to the failures.
